entities.name: Ma'at (Cosmic Order)
entities.label: Idea
entities.summary: The central ethical and cosmological concept of ancient Egyptian civilization, personified as a goddess wearing an ostrich feather. Ma'at represented truth, justice, cosmic order, balance, and right conduct — the fundamental principle by which the universe functioned and by which human society should be governed. The pharaoh's primary duty was to uphold Ma'at; the judgment of the dead consisted of weighing the heart against the feather of Ma'at. It pervaded every aspect of Egyptian life: law, governance, religious ritual, and personal ethics. Ma'at is one of the earliest articulations of a universal moral order in human thought.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ma'at's influence on ancient Egyptian civilization shaped their understanding of truth, justice, and right conduct, with far-reaching consequences for governance, law, and personal ethics. Its impact can be seen in the pharaonic system and the judgment of the dead, where the heart was weighed against the feather of Ma'at.
